---
title: "Continue, test, and challenge a research plan"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%", dpi = 144)
library(suppose)
```

A reviewed model supports several different questions: where to measure next,
what future result would challenge its prediction, and whether changing an
assumption changes the recommendation. Each has its own review. Saving a planning
choice does not freeze a prediction or run an experiment.

This executable example uses an invented coating dataset. Its results provide
no evidence about a real material. The optional alloptr design engine is needed
for the planning sections.

```{r example}
record <- suppose_worked_example("regression", seed = 1)
model <- tail(record$regressions, 1)[[1]]
contrast <- data.frame(temperature = c(140, 160), duration = 60)
```

## Continue a reviewed plan

In **Record > Plan the next measurement**, choose a saved plan and click
**Start draft from reviewed plan**. This restores its actual candidates, target,
costs, budget and preference. Populated forms require an explicit replacement.
The comparison stays visible while the CSV and numerical controls sit under
**Adjust candidate settings and assumptions**.

Ask chat to change one assumption, such as the cost of one experiment. Other
settings are preserved. If you edit the form while chat works, the incoming draft
waits for you to choose whether to use it. Every revised plan needs a new
comparison and review, and points back to the original planning review. A model
from an earlier claim revision must be reviewed for the current claim first.

```{r plan, eval=requireNamespace("alloptr", quietly=TRUE)}
candidates <- data.frame(
  candidate_id = c("low", "high"),
  temperature = c(140, 160), duration = 60,
  repeats = 6, cost = 0, feasible = TRUE
)
comparison <- design_regression(
  record, model$id, candidates, contrast,
  rationale = "Invented independent preparations; explicitly omit costs."
)
record <- record_research_design(
  record, comparison, comparison$recommended[1],
  "Tutorial analyst", "Review the synthetic learning comparison", reviewed = TRUE
)
first_plan <- record$research_designs[[1]]
settings <- research_design_settings(record, first_plan$id)
settings$candidates$cost[2] <- 0.01
revised <- do.call(design_regression, c(list(x = record), settings))
record <- record_research_design(
  record, revised, revised$recommended[1],
  "Tutorial analyst", "Change only high-temperature experiment cost", reviewed = TRUE
)
stopifnot(identical(record$research_designs[[1]], first_plan))
```

## Challenge a frozen prediction

With a chosen regression, `/test` opens **A future regression test**. Plan the
exact future IDs, predictor settings in original units, collection protocol,
assignment procedure, deadline and assessment rule. Review the computed
prediction and confirm independent units and unexamined outcomes before freezing.
Chat can prepare the form; the person freezes it.

Two rules are available:

| Rule | What is assessed | Uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| `joint_outcomes` | All planned outcomes in one joint region | Joint coefficient uncertainty and unknown common noise; one simultaneous check |
| `mean_difference` | Future sample mean B minus A | A Student-t interval including future measurement noise |

A population mean is unobserved. Its uncertainty is narrower than the uncertainty
of a future sample mean difference. Neither rule checks independent marginal
intervals as if they were a simultaneous region. Both require the complete
planned cohort; missing outcomes cannot silently change the statistic.

Here the six measurements form a separate two-setting test. A linked research
plan must instead match its chosen single setting and replicate count exactly;
a declined plan cannot create a commitment.

```{r freeze}
planned <- data.frame(
  observation_id = paste0("future-", 1:6),
  condition = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
  temperature = rep(c(140, 160), each = 3), duration = 60
)
deadline <- format(Sys.time() + 7 * 86400, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")
preview <- plan_regression_test(
  record, model$id, planned,
  source = "fictional:future-coating", protocol = "independent-randomized-v1",
  horizon = deadline, target = "Fixed-time temperature contrast",
  design = "intervention",
  design_details = "Invented independent batches with randomized assignment and oven order.",
  rule = "mean_difference"
)
preview$prediction$contrast[c("mean", "lower", "upper")]
record <- commit_regression_test(
  record, preview, "Tutorial analyst", "Freeze before generating the fictional outcomes",
  independent = TRUE, outcomes_unseen = TRUE
)
commitment <- tail(record$regression_commitments, 1)[[1]]
```

## Attach outcomes and preserve corrections

Download the measurement template from the frozen test. Fill in actual settings,
outcomes, independent-unit identities and observation times. Declare actual
source, protocol and units; the template's planned values are not proof of what
happened. Review the uploaded table before attaching it, then preview and retain
an assessment.

The example generates fictional outcomes **after** freezing. It is a software
rehearsal, not a scientific validation.

```{r collect}
future <- planned
future$outcome <- 54 + 0.4 * (future$temperature - 150) + c(-1, 0, 1, 1, -1, 0)
future$batch <- future$observation_id
future$specimen <- future$observation_id
future$observed_at <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS6Z", tz = "UTC")
record <- record_regression_test_data(
  record, commitment$id, future,
  source = "fictional:future-coating", protocol = "independent-randomized-v1",
  units = "MPa", predictor_units = c(temperature = "degC", duration = "minutes"),
  author = "Tutorial analyst", reason = "Invented future measurements",
  outcomes_unseen = TRUE
)
record <- assess_regression_test(
  record, commitment$id, "Tutorial analyst", "Review the complete fictional cohort",
  protocol_followed = TRUE
)
tail(record$regression_assessments, 1)[[1]]$status
```

Before the deadline, incomplete cohorts await outcomes. After the deadline they
are inconclusive. Wrong settings, mismatched units or protocols, repeated units,
unknown times, outcomes before freezing, and outcomes after the deadline prevent
an eligible assessment. Declarations do not authenticate collection or establish
causality.

A correction names the active attachment in `supersedes` and contains exactly its
IDs. This retains the earlier measurements and assessments. A new assessment
references the corrected evidence versions. Revising the claim or fitting a
later model does not change the frozen prediction.

## Check dependence on model and decision assumptions

With a chosen regression, `/sensitivity` opens **Regression and design
sensitivity**. Choose a two-setting mean contrast and powers for the joint prior,
likelihood, or both separately. Review changes in the contrast interval, the
probability of a scientifically meaningful gain, noise, predictive checks and,
optionally, a saved plan's candidate benefits and recommendations.

```{r sensitivity}
comparison <- sensitivity_regression(
  record, model$id, contrast, meaningful_gain = 8,
  powers = c(0.8, 1, 1.25), draws = 200, seed = 1
)
do.call(rbind, lapply(comparison$variants, function(v) {
  data.frame(component = v$component, power = v$power,
    mean = v$contrast$mean, probability_above_8 = v$contrast$probability_above,
    review_flag = v$review_flag)
}))
record <- record_regression_sensitivity(
  record, comparison, "Tutorial analyst",
  "Inspect the consequences of changing each assumption", reviewed = TRUE
)
```

These powers act on the full joint prior density in coefficients and variance,
or on the full likelihood. They are not replacements for alternative scientific
models, and do not mean multiplying a coefficient's marginal SD. Improper powered
priors are rejected. Each posterior is solved exactly; predictive checks retain
finite simulation uncertainty and use the original measurement model.

To include a saved research plan, supply its entry ID as `design_id`. Candidate
settings, costs, feasibility and budget stay fixed. For a decision-purpose plan,
`utility_thresholds` changes only the stated preference under the original
posterior. It is separate from `meaningful_gain`, the scientific threshold. Equal
best scores at numerical resolution remain tied; an empty recommendation means
no positive net benefit.

Power scaling follows the component-wise definition in the
[priorsense guide](https://n-kall.github.io/priorsense/articles/powerscaling.html).
Suppose solves this bounded conjugate family directly rather than applying
importance sampling. A few unflagged perturbations do not establish robustness.
See [the mathematical methods](methods.html) for the parameterization.

## Save and reopen

```{r save}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_record(record, path)
reopened <- read_record(path)
stopifnot(identical(reopened$regression_commitments[[1]]$id, commitment$id))
length(reopened$regression_assessments)
```

With [history turned on](workbench.html#return-to-your-work), the app's native
history retains the conversation, reviewed plans, frozen tests, measurement
versions, assessments and sensitivity reviews. Downloaded records are portable
copies. Pending chat drafts reopen as suggestions, with no restored review
confirmation or execution authority.
